findings.title: Blanket `*.jsonl` / `*.log` ignores set the local-green / CI-red trap for test fixtures
findings.note: The blanket *.jsonl and *.log patterns match at any depth, so a fixture checked into tests/ would be silently un-committable and invisible to the several tests that scan the git-tracked tree. Latent: no such fixture exists yet.

findings.title: Dead constructs, one of which contradicts the guard it describes
findings.note: Dead constructs in the ingestion area, including the one that matters: exclude.validate_bpf_expr is documented as the guard against a filter that matches everything and yields an empty-but-healthy capture, and it is unreachable while the shipped filter is a shell re-implementation in the k8s manifest.

findings.title: The capability check proves less than it claims
findings.note: The in-container check proves only that the effective capability set is non-zero while its comment and message claim a NET_RAW verification, so a container with NET_ADMIN alone passes and Zeek dies at capture. The bit-test idiom already exists 11 lines earlier in the same file.

findings.title: The GUI manifest contradicts itself about how the Workloads panel gets data
findings.note: The GUI manifest asserts both that it ships no kubectl and that it needs kubectl to list workloads, while the panel that paragraph explains was deleted from the frontend; the paragraph is stale in both directions.

findings.title: Unqualified image references only resolve on nodes that already have them
findings.note: The shipped default references an unqualified image name the project never publishes, so it resolves only where install.sh already imported the local build; IfNotPresent makes the difference invisible on the node that works.

findings.title: The GUI receives Pushover credentials it has no use for
findings.note: A NodePort-authenticated HTTP pod holds the Pushover user key and API token to render a set/not-set row it does not need the value for, while the only process that sends a push is the worker.

findings.title: busybox `nc -z` in the GUI init may not exist
findings.note: nc -z exists and works in the pinned busybox 1.37, verified by pulling the official image's binary and running it (--help lists -z). The real defect in the same invocation is that it omits -w, so the bounded loop's fallback depends on the connection failing fast rather than on the iteration count.

findings.title: `_file_identity`'s size and mtime are never compared — the documented replacement protection is thinner than claimed
findings.note: The mtime element of the identity tuple is discarded and prev_size is never read, so the same-inode/same-size replacement the docstring says is caught is not caught by the identity at all. Duplicates the already-CONFIRMED F066.

findings.title: Zeek tail-state dict grows without bound for the life of the process
findings.note: Nothing removes a key from the Zeek tail-state dict and it lives for the life of the process, growing by roughly one entry per rotated filename. Small in magnitude but the bound is absent rather than generous.

findings.title: A numeric `etype` silently becomes 2048 (IPv4)
findings.note: Any etype that is not one of two known strings is silently recorded as 2048, including numeric 34525 and goflow2's real ARP/unknown outputs. Inert only because nothing reads the column; the adjacent proto field already handles the numeric case.

findings.title: Table names are hardcoded `weirvern.*` while `CLICKHOUSE_DB` is a configurable setting
findings.note: CLICKHOUSE_DB is honoured for the connection binding and the unqualified CREATE statements and ignored by every SELECT/INSERT and by half the schema files, so a non-default value splits the dataset and fails schema application loudly - while the CLI advertises the knob.

findings.title: NetFlow-only deployments get a "check your Zeek sensor" warning every five minutes, forever
findings.note: The 'Zeek summary is empty' warning fires on every detection sweep (300s by default) on every NetFlow-only deployment, because emptiness is the expected state there and no guard consults the deployment's configuration; the same file latches its other steady-state warning.

findings.title: heartbeat_interval_s is not validated against the staleness threshold
findings.note: heartbeat_interval_s is bounded only below, so a value above the staleness threshold makes every beat arrive already stale and a healthy sensor report as NOT RUNNING; the invariant exists only as a test assertion against the shipped default.

findings.title: Settings help says the ClickHouse default user is 'weirvern'; the code default is 'default'
findings.note: The Settings help for clickhouse_user states a default the code does not use and attributes the user to a schema Job that creates no user at all - it is created by the ClickHouse entrypoint from the ConfigMap value.

findings.title: The viewer Role's `pods/portforward create` contradicts its "read-only" framing
findings.note: pods/portforward create is granted namespace-wide with no resourceNames (create cannot be name-scoped), and two of the namespace's pods are hostNetwork, so the read-only identity can reach node-level listeners. Raised to MEDIUM.

findings.title: Raw exception text is returned to HTTP clients
findings.note: Exception text reaches response bodies unscrubbed on the catch-alls and the data and API routes, carrying ClickHouse error bodies that name tables and SQL fragments, and the API server's own rejection detail.

findings.title: `arp_sweep` can report a false empty network by two mechanisms
findings.note: Both mechanisms exist: an empty source raises inside the builder, which is the exact OSError the send loop swallows, and a 0.0.0.0 source builds a request nothing answers. find_free_addresses then offers the whole network as free and the CLI says intercepting it would affect nobody.

findings.title: `liveness()` returning `None` is rendered as "no evidence — check the overlay", breaking the probe's own stated contract
findings.note: liveness() or {} collapses the documented None return into 'no evidence', and the one note that fires blames the overlay - a diagnosis the probe never measured. The three-state reasoning it should copy is already written twice in this tree.

findings.title: `intercept_running` renders an unreadable child state as "not running"
findings.note: A poll() that raises returns False, the same value as a clean exit, and that False also hands the heartbeat row back to the worker, so an unreadable child reads as a stopped intercept on every surface.

findings.title: `ForwardingState.rule_installed` / `table_installed` are never written
findings.note: Both fields are declared and defaulted but written by nothing, so the stress harness's 'report what is left' teardown check prints rule=False table=False whatever the routing table actually holds. The real answers exist in forwarding_path_problems.

findings.title: A successful survey whose log cannot be read is reported as "the survey produced no output"
findings.note: A survey job that SUCCEEDED but whose pod log could not be fetched is raised as 'the survey produced no output', pointing the operator at the segment instead of at the read failure. Reproduced against the suite's own fake cluster.

findings.title: `sweep_probe`'s borrowed address leaks on SIGKILL — state left on the node's capture NIC
findings.note: The borrowed address is withdrawn only in a finally and the probe carries no deadline or backstop, so SIGKILL leaves an address on the node's capture NIC that the calling harness's cleanup does not cover.

findings.title: `sweep_probe` defaults the interface to `eth1` one line after refusing a default segment
findings.note: The interface gets an eth1 default one line after the segment refuses a default, and in the current tree the segment refusal always fires first, so the probe cannot sweep anywhere - reproduced with INTERCEPT_SEGMENT set in the environment.

findings.title: The envFrom handling is a dead assert plus a skip that abandons the regression check
findings.note: The pod-level envFrom assert compares a field that does not exist at pod scope, so it cannot fire on any API-valid manifest; and the pytest.skip below it retires the MGMT_IFACE regression check the moment any container in that pod gains envFrom - a form six other workloads here already use. Measured: 1 skipped, exit 0.

findings.title: The startup-script scan reads only `args` and passes vacuously on an empty script
findings.note: The startup-script scan reads only args, so the equally valid command: ['/bin/sh','-c',<script>] form yields an empty string and the test passes having examined zero variables, with no non-vacuity guard anywhere.

findings.title: The no-TLS boundary test is satisfied by the docstring it says is insufficient
findings.note: 'TLS' in the module source is satisfied by the phrase 'terminate TLS', so deleting the no-TLS statement leaves the test green - the exact 'documented only where developers look' failure the test names.

findings.title: The installer guards pin one spelling of the fix, and one requires the comment to survive
findings.note: Both installer guards match text rather than behaviour: one demands the literal token 'empty' and the -n spelling, the other an exact comment string and one operand order, so a correct re-wording or an equivalent edit turns the suite red.

findings.title: The ZEEKPATH guard misses the `ENV name value` form
findings.note: The ZEEKPATH guard matches the literal ZEEKPATH= only, so the ENV name value form - which still sets the variable - passes the check that exists to forbid it. Latent: the image sets no ENV today.

findings.title: The service-CIDR scrubber guard pins one regex spelling of the removed rule
findings.note: The guard greps source text for one regex spelling, so [.] escaping, a whole-range pattern, a non-raw string or a differently indented line re-introduces the rule while the test stays green. The product's own scrub_text is what should be asserted on.

findings.title: The identity MAC-clause check is satisfied by the wrong column
findings.note: split(SELECT, 1) lands inside a comment that names SELECT, so the assertion is satisfied by prose; it also accepts any column containing 'mac' and never checks the positional unpack, so a SELECT reorder binds the wrong column and stays green. Four mutations passed.

findings.title: Two manifest tests are blind to CronJob-shaped workloads
findings.note: Both manifest tests iterate four workload kinds and omit CronJob, so the prune job's pod spec is never selected: a key-less required configMapKeyRef and runAsUser 0 both pass with no test noticing.

findings.title: Stray `before=""` parameter; the settings-route floor of 15
findings.note: One test carries an unused defaulted parameter, and the settings-route check asserts a floor of 15 against 19 advertised keys, so four keys can stop rendering a row before the regression test fails.

findings.title: The per-request token re-read check inspects only `do_POST`
findings.note: The per-request token check slices one 16-line do_POST shim, so a re-read added to _authorize (14 call sites on the write path) or to _route_post is invisible to it, and the GET path is not examined at all.

findings.title: Text-parsing fragility in the sanitation checks
findings.note: The .gitignore checks are substring tests satisfied by the comment naming the patterns, so all three real rules can be deleted with the test green; and git ls-files is whitespace-split, so a space-containing tracked path fragments and hides. The correct -z parse already exists in a sibling file.

findings.title: The x509 arm of the protocol union is dropped by the only reader shown in the bundle
findings.note: The x509 arm emits an empty host key and index_protocol_records drops exactly those rows, so the table is collected and unread while two separate guards report it as reachable. Live on every sweep.

findings.title: The fifth JA4 exposure carries sentinels unfiltered
findings.note: The protocol union's ssl arm selects ja4 raw, so the two historical sentinels count as TLS sessions and dilute the T1573 denominator: 1 real plus 9 sentinel suppresses a genuine downgrade ratio entirely. The sentinel filter is applied in four places and omitted from the fifth.

findings.title: `baseline_ja4_set` is capped at an arbitrary 64; the window set is uncapped
findings.note: The baseline fingerprint set is capped at 64 while the window set it is compared against is uncapped, so for a host with more distinct client builds some familiar fingerprints read as novelty. Latent until the ja4 baseline is wired up.

findings.title: "Absent" rows can still carry SSH/HTTP/files values
findings.note: The presence flag sums five logs while the keys CTE unions twelve, and the pass-through list is copied before the presence decision, so a row can carry zeek_present 0 with real ssh/http/file values in the same feature vector. Live on every sweep.

findings.title: Two baseline columns have no reader in the bundle
findings.note: baseline_conn_count and the ja4 baseline's ssl_count are emitted by queries whose docstring says what they are for, and no consumer reads either; the guards around them assert the NAME appears in the SQL text rather than that a value is used.

findings.title: The DBSCAN ordering contract is impossible as written
findings.note: The helper advertises one column order serving both ZEEK_FEATURES and ZEEK_DBSCAN_FEATURES, which is impossible for those two lists, and the tests guarding it are self-slices that pass for any ordering. The live DBSCAN query is correct only because it bypasses the helper.

findings.title: Partial per-block aggregates blinded T1046/T1018: every discovery threshold counted one insert block, not the window
findings.note: CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE CLUSTER, then fixed. A ClickHouse materialized view fires PER INSERT BLOCK, so every insert into weirvern.flows writes its own aggregate row for the same (window_start, src_addr); the target tables are MergeTree(), not ReplacingMergeTree, so those partial rows are NEVER merged. MEASURED over 24h: flows_aggregated 592 host-windows with 555 fragmented (93.8%), worst case 46 rows; flows_aggregated_diversity 589/552 (93.7%), also 46 worst case. One worst-case window's 46 partial rows held unique_dst_ports of [1,1,1,2,1,1,...2]: the sweep saw (max) 2 ports while the window held (sum) 81. TWO failures compounded: `flows` was one dict PER PARTIAL ROW (up to 46 scorer inputs for one host-window), and `flow_by_key`'s plain dict assignment meant the LAST partial won -- typically the smallest block, so T1046's port threshold was evaluated against the least informative row of the window. A 500-port scan spread over 46 insert blocks read as 1-2 ports, below every discovery threshold. FIXED by folding partials into ONE row per host-window before scoring: additive columns summed, cardinalities RE-DERIVED FROM THE RAW FLOW TABLE (summing partials is an upper bound, and an inflated count that gates a scan rule manufactures false positives -- trading a gap for false positives is not a fix). A THIRD, DEEPER CASE WAS FOUND BY MEASURING RATHER THAN REASONING: port_entropy is a per-block measurement that CANNOT be recovered by folding at all -- entropy over 2 ports is bounded by log2(2)=1.0 however many blocks are added, while T1046 requires 3.0. Live per-block entropy on fragmented windows measured 0 to 0.54. So entropy, stddev and active_minutes are RECOMPUTED from raw flows using the materialized view's own expressions, including its `dst_port > 0` filter so both paths describe the same population. The raw-read failure path falls back to summing and LOGS that the counts are an upper bound, because a silently approximate threshold is how this hid. VERIFIED against the real code on the deployed cluster with a synthetic 300-port scan arriving in 60 small blocks: the old path mapped NOTHING (5 ports seen), the fixed path maps T1046 + T1595 + T1018 with the evidence reading '300 distinct destination ports (threshold 100), port entropy 7.90 (threshold 3.0)'. Live sweeps show 0 fallback warnings, so cardinalities are exact. 11 tests, 7 mutations caught -- including two that were MISSED first (deleting entropy from the SELECT, and dropping the dst_port > 0 filter) because every other test replaces db.fetch_rows_named wholesale and never examines the SQL the product issues; a query-text test now pins those.

findings.title: Train and score encoded the day of week on different calendars: ClickHouse toDayOfWeek (Mon=1) vs Python weekday() (Mon=0)
findings.note: CONFIRMED AGAINST CLICKHOUSE ITSELF, then fixed and deployed. This is the '7-feature train/score scale mismatch' recorded as an open high-severity item. The training queries in models/detectors.py encode the day of week with ClickHouse's `toDayOfWeek`, which is Monday=1 through Sunday=7; `features.extract_features` encoded the SAME window with Python's `datetime.weekday()`, which is Monday=0 through Sunday=6 -- a constant off-by-one on the day index. MEASURED against the cluster for a Wednesday window, which both sides agree is index 3 vs 2: from ClickHouse dow_sin 0.43388373911755823 / dow_cos -0.900968867902419; from the module dow_sin 0.9749279121818236 / dow_cos -0.22252093395631434. So the model learned one point on the weekly circle and was asked to score another: the model was not wrong, it was answering a different question. Nothing raised, because the vector had the right LENGTH and every value was a valid number -- the silent class this campaign keeps finding. The `is_business_hours` predicate was CONSISTENT on both sides (ClickHouse `< 6` and Python `< 5` both mean Mon-Fri), so only the cyclic pair was wrong; the fix moves the whole encoding to `isoweekday()` and restates the predicate as `< 6` on the same number the query uses, so the two halves cannot sit on different calendars. FIXED IN features.py; VERIFIED in the running container: 14 of 14 features now agree to 4.44e-16. THE ARTIFACTS NEEDED RETRAINING, and this is the part worth remembering: the persisted IF/GB/DBSCAN pickles were fit at 03:54 on the old encoding, and because scoring uses the LIVE feature list and the artifact's own fitted preprocessor, a corrected encoder plus a stale artifact is STILL mismatched in both directions. The three artifacts were renamed to .premismatch (not deleted, so a rollback is possible) and the worker was restarted; it trained cold at 09:37 (Isolation Forest on 80000 samples, anomaly rate 3.300%). 11 tests, 6 mutations caught -- including two CROSS-FILE mutations changing the training SQL itself, which is the drift this defect was. MY OWN ERROR: my first transcription of ClickHouse's outputs for days 4 and 5 was wrong in the last two digits and the test passed anyway because the tolerance was 1e-9; the values are now quoted verbatim from a live query rather than re-derived in Python, which would have compared the module against the same mistake a second time.

findings.title: Every worker restart re-read all Zeek logs, and for the tables with no dedup key that multiplied model inputs (notice_count 64x)
findings.note: CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE CLUSTER, then fixed. Found while refuting the above. `tail_zeek_dir` kept its per-log cursors in a DICT IN MEMORY (keyed by filename), so every worker restart re-read all Zeek logs from offset zero. The NetFlow tailer got a persisted cursor in F018; this path never did. THE COST WAS NOT STARTUP WORK, which is what the code's own docstring assumed: `zeek_notice` and `zeek_dhcp` are plain `MergeTree` with NO dedup key, because their `uid` is EMPTY -- they cannot be `ReplacingMergeTree ORDER BY (ts, uid)` the way `zeek_conn`/`zeek_dns` are. A re-read therefore ADDS instead of collapsing. MEASURED: zeek_notice held 6556 rows for 162 distinct (ts, note, msg) groups with single rows appearing 64 times; zeek_dhcp 3201 rows for 65 distinct (ts, mac) with rows appearing 47 times. And `zeek_features.py` aggregates those tables with plain count(), so `zeek_notice_count` read 64 where the truth was 1 -- a 64x inflation of a LIVE MODEL INPUT, growing with every restart. FIXED by persisting the cursor per log file, with a dedicated `load_zeek_state`/`save_zeek_state` pair because the Zeek cursor must carry the parsed `#fields` header alongside the offset: a Zeek data line is positional, so an offset restored without its field names maps nothing. The checkpoint reuses the F018 path helper (MODEL_DIR, writable, survives restarts) and inherits its rotation revalidation. VERIFIED: a simulated restart now ingests 0 from an unchanged file (was: everything), still ingests exactly the 2 rows appended while it was down, and a rotation is still caught rather than trusted. 5 tests, 6 mutations caught. A SECOND DEFECT WAS FOUND IN MY OWN FIRST VERSION: I called `save_tail_state` and then patched the header into the same file, but `save_tail_state` writes a FRESH payload and atomically replaces the file, so it wiped the header written a moment earlier and only the ordering decided which keys survived. The payload is now built and written once. MY TEST WAS ALSO WRONG: I asserted the separator with an INVENTED comma-separated Zeek log; real Zeek always writes '#separator \x09' (verified on every log on the sensor), so that fixture described a file that does not exist. LIMITATION, MEASURED AND STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the live deployment has 367 Zeek files but the tailer's `depth=50` bound per type per pass means checkpoints accumulate across passes, so the first restart after this fix still re-read a large set of previously-unechecked rotated files. The fix removes the re-read for everything checkpointed and stops the multiplication going forward; it does not retroactively clean the rows already duplicated, which is left as an operator decision.

findings.title: Host identification had no input for 20 hours and every health probe read green: nothing measured the fingerprint feed
findings.note: CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE CLUSTER, then fixed. `host_fingerprints` is the input to host identification (the raw MAC-vendor/DHCP-hostname/JA4/software observations that `build_identity` classifies). MEASURED: newest observation 72,837s old = 20.2 hours, while EVERY probe on the health page read green. NOTHING in the admin surface reads that table -- `grep -c host_fingerprints weirvern/admin/*.py` returns nothing -- and the probe that looks like it covers this, `identity`, reports COVERAGE from the VERDICT table, which shrinks slowly as hosts age out of a 7-day window, so a dead feed looks like a stable deployment for most of a week. The reported symptom was `_record_observations` logging dropped rows at DEBUG. THAT LOGGING IS CORRECT AND IS NOT THE FIX: identification is enrichment, and losing flow data to report a fingerprint problem would trade the important thing for the useful one. The real defect is the MISSING MEASUREMENT -- if failures are deliberately quiet, something must measure the result, or a total outage and a quiet segment are indistinguishable. FIXED with a `fingerprint_feed` probe on the age of the newest observation, tri-state like zeek_freshness so a NetFlow-only deployment (no Zeek sensor, correctly no observations) reports ok=None with a detail naming both cases. THE THRESHOLD IS MEASURED, NOT PICKED: my first version used 24h on the reasoning that a quiet segment produces nothing for hours, and deploying it at 20h17m of real staleness still reported `ok` -- a bound that only fires after the failure has run most of a day is barely a probe. Measured healthy gaps are median 73s, p90 212s, p99 2,277s, so the bound is 4h: an order of magnitude above p99 and well below the measured stall, with a test pinning it between those two measured values. VERIFIED LIVE: every other probe green, overall ok False, row reads '[FAIL] fingerprint_feed newest observation 20h20m ago (5872 in 7d)'. 4 tests, 6 mutations caught. THE UNDERLYING STALL IS NOT A CODE DEFECT and is recorded as such: each source's newest observation coincides EXACTLY with the newest log file of its type (ja4 13:46 vs ssl.*.log, software 13:24, dhcp 12:48 vs dhcp.*.log), while Zeek rotates dns/conn/stats/notice/capture_loss hourly through today and writes NO rotations for dhcp, ssl or software -- those three analyzers produce nothing on this segment. Two unconfirmed candidates: the capture interface is a veth that may not carry DHCP/TLS broadcast traffic, and the site policy's 'dhcp ALREADY WRITING' comment was true when written.

findings.title: Every window below min_flows_for_full_confidence is mathematically unalertable: the damping floor (a multiplier) is below base_threshold (an absolute score) divided by the score cap
findings.note: CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE CLUSTER, then fixed. FOUND BY FOLLOWING A BATCH RESULT: after the sweep was restored, every near miss scored EXACTLY 0.3465 -- 23 of 23, across six unrelated hosts -- against a threshold of 0.35. A constant score across unrelated hosts is not a coincidence, it is an arithmetic ceiling. `fuse_scores` caps every score at 0.99; `detection_confidence_factor` multiplies by max(thin_window_floor, flow_count/min_flows_for_full_confidence). For a 1-3 flow window that ratio is 0.1-0.3, so the floor applies: 0.99 * 0.35 = 0.3465, which is 0.0035 SHORT of the 0.35 bar. A one-flow window where EVERY detector reported the maximum was therefore suppressed, and no input could change that -- the window was not scored low, it was UNREACHABLE. MEASURED: 566 of 567 windows in a 6-hour span (99.8%, carrying 99.98% of the bytes) were thin enough to be capped there. THE INSTRUMENT WAS CHECKED BEFORE THE FINDING WAS TRUSTED: counts were read from the COLLAPSED per-window aggregates via _collapse_partial_aggregates, because F181 established the raw table is fragmented per insert block and a per-block read would have understated them -- after collapsing, 25 of 25 windows were still under min_flows_for_full_confidence. MY OWN MEASUREMENT HAD TO BE CORRECTED TWICE (I first selected unique_dst_ports from flows_aggregated, where it does not exist, then joined a non-existent flows_diversity table), so the verification now reads the schema's own table names. THE ROOT CAUSE IS TWO DIFFERENT KINDS OF NUMBER SHARING ONE VALUE: thin_window_floor is a MULTIPLIER on a capped score and base_threshold is an ABSOLUTE score, and both shipped as 0.35, which hid the relationship. FIXED: the cap is now the named constant MAX_FUSED_SCORE, a new assert_thin_floor_is_reachable(cfg, base_threshold) makes the relationship CHECKED rather than implied, and thin_window_floor is 0.36 -- the smallest value that clears the bar with margin (0.99*0.36 = 0.3564) while keeping the measured false-positive case suppressed (a 3-flow window with raw 0.96 still lands at 0.3456, below the bar). TWO CALL SITES, DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT: main() RAISES (SystemExit 2) next to the malformed-CIDR precedent, so a deployment that could never have alerted refuses to start; the sweep logs ONCE PER CONFIGURATION via a latch, because BASE_THRESHOLD is operator-editable on a running cluster (0.0-1.0) and raising from inside the loop would replace 'blind to thin windows' with 'detection stops entirely', which is strictly worse. TESTS: 11 added. MUTATION TESTING CAUGHT TWO OF MY OWN TEST DEFECTS: the latch test RE-IMPLEMENTED the latch inside the test, so removing the product's latch changed nothing -- the logic was extracted to check_thin_floor_reachable so the test drives real code; and a mutation of the startup exit code hit the WRONG SITE because two identical 'raise SystemExit(2) from exc' lines exist (the CIDR check and this one). 8 mutations, 8 caught after both were fixed. VERIFIED LIVE: the shipped config is ACCEPTED with a reachable ceiling of 0.3564, the old 0.35 floor is REFUSED, and the worker logs no unalertable warning. POST-FIX LIVE EVIDENCE, and it separates the two gates cleanly: the pre-restart rows read 0.3465 (= 0.99 * 0.35, the old floor) with reason=below-threshold, and the post-restart rows read 0.3564 (= 0.99 * 0.36, the new floor) with reason=near-miss-band on the SCORE being above the bar -- so the arithmetic impossibility is gone and thin windows now reach the threshold. Their remaining suppression is the AGREEMENT gate (model_agreement 0.25 against min_agreement 0.33), which is a separate, deliberate corroboration requirement and NOT part of this finding. HONEST LIMIT: no thin window has yet produced an ALERT on this segment, because the windows that are thin also happen to have a single detector firing, so the corroboration gate still holds them; this fix removes the category-level impossibility, it does not by itself make those specific windows alert-worthy. Also confirmed incidentally that F043's denominator holds live: every model_agreement value over 6h is a multiple of 0.25 (27 at 0.25, 18 at 0.5, 102 at 0.75, 8 at 1.0), which is the 4-detector ensemble, not the survivors.
